items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: like Benny Goodman and all of that. The jukeboxes would be loaded with that kind of music.

ctx.x: Do you recall if the music that you were getting into, were your parents using the word “jazz” or was it just the music that was in the house?

Well I mean first of all I was 4 years old when it started so I don’t know if it was swing or big band. I can’t really recall the word “jazz” until later on. We moved to Buffalo in 1949, and that’s when the jazz started to come into play. But I mean as I would call it, it was like the big band era, the swing era you know, like Benny Goodman and all of that. The jukeboxes would be loaded with that kind of music. “Stardust,” and “I Can’t Get Started With You,” and “Begin the Beguine” with Artie Shaw, and all of…
So by the time you were in like junior high school, had you decided on your career path so to speak?
